cases.provider_identity: GeneratedHostApp Phoenix endpoint from source checkout, mounted at /lockspire; no package receipt.

input_identity.request: Authorization Code request uses https://client.example.com/callback/ while the synthetic client registered https://client.example.com/callback.

cases.auth_mode: synthetic public client; rejection precedes host authentication
cases.safe_condition: A trailing-slash mismatch is an invalid redirect URI.

normative_references.basis: An invalid Redirection URI must not receive an error redirect.

support_reference.claim: Phase 37 strictness slice includes exact redirect_uri matching.

cases.observed_outcome: HTTP 400 first-party error; no Location header.
cases.expected_outcome: Reject the mismatched URI without redirecting the user agent to it.
cases.cause_detail: The current source-host test matched the exact-match safety expectation; no current protocol defect was reproduced.

repro.test_name: exact redirect_uri mismatches stay on the browser-safe surface

cases.disposition: Current deterministic proof supports this one unsafe-callback boundary; it makes no valid-callback package or certification claim.

cases.family: valid callback error/state and query encoding
cases.provider_identity: Lockspire.Web.Router test host with configured issuer https://issuer.test/lockspire and /lockspire mount.

input_identity.request: Registered callback https://client.example.com/callback?foo=bar&state=old-state plus a safe validation error; synthetic client values.

cases.profile: authorization code; default query response mode
cases.safe_condition: The callback is the exact registered URI including its query component; new OAuth error/state fields are encoded without replacing unrelated query data or trusting stale state.

normative_references.basis: For a valid Redirection URI, return the appropriate error and state parameters.

support_reference.claim: Authorization code is supported with exact redirect URI matching.

cases.observed_outcome: 302/303 to the registered callback; foo=bar and state=state-123 remain, error=invalid_request is present, and state=old-state is absent.
cases.expected_outcome: Return the OAuth error and current state through the exact valid callback while preserving unrelated registered query data.
cases.cause_detail: The focused controller test passed for this exact registered callback and query condition.

repro.test_name: redirect-safe validation failures merge existing redirect query params canonically

cases.disposition: Existing deterministic proof is reused; callback mismatch policy remains unchanged.

cases.provider_identity: Lockspire.Web.Router source-host test host configured with the synthetic issuer and /lockspire consent mount.

input_identity.request: Valid registered authorization-code request with scope openid email, state, nonce and S256; candidate changes only response_mode to binary.

cases.safe_condition: Response mode is unsupported, so the server cannot safely encode the error using that mode.

normative_references.basis: An unsupported Response Mode requires HTTP 400 without Error Response parameters.

support_reference.claim: Only repo-proven authorization-code and response representations are claimed.

cases.observed_outcome: HTTP 302 to the registered callback with error, error_description, iss, and state parameters.
cases.expected_outcome: HTTP 400 without OAuth Error Response parameters for unsupported response_mode.
cases.cause_detail: The controlled request reached the named final assertion; the source returned a registered-callback redirect with OAuth error parameters instead of HTTP 400 without them.

repro.test_name: A171-003 valid direct consent control then requires unsupported mode to be HTTP 400 without OAuth error parameters
repro.reason: The controlled request reached the named final assertion; the source returned a registered-callback redirect with OAuth error parameters instead of HTTP 400 without them.

cases.disposition: A current supported normative failure was reproduced with valid controls; carry it as correction input to the downstream owner.

cases.provider_identity: GeneratedHostApp Phoenix endpoint with host-owned account resolver and session, mounted at /lockspire.

input_identity.request: Public code+PKCE request uses prompt=none without a visible host session.

cases.profile: OIDC authorization code with host-owned sessions
cases.auth_mode: public client with PKCE S256; no host session
cases.safe_condition: prompt=none must not display or redirect into host login when the user is not silently authenticated.

normative_references.basis: With prompt=none the Authorization Server must not interact and must return an error when the user cannot be silently authenticated.
login_required is an allowed error for an unsatisfied prompt=none request.

support_reference.claim: The Phase 37 strictness slice includes prompt=none returning redirect-safe login_required.

cases.observed_outcome: 302/303 to the registered callback with login_required and original state; no host /login redirect.
cases.expected_outcome: Return redirect-safe login_required without interactive host login.
cases.cause_detail: The deterministic host integration test passed for the no-session case.

repro.test_name: prompt=none with no visible host session returns login_required without host login redirection

cases.disposition: Existing deterministic source-host proof is reused; host session policy remains host-owned.

cases.provider_identity: GeneratedHostApp endpoint uses host-owned current_account_id and current_auth_time_unix session fields.

input_identity.request: Authenticated host session has auth_time 600 seconds old; request uses max_age=60 and prompt=none.

cases.profile: OIDC authorization code with host-owned session freshness
cases.auth_mode: public client with PKCE S256 and a stale host session
cases.safe_condition: The configured host resolver's old authentication time exceeds the request's max_age.

normative_references.basis: The OP must attempt active reauthentication when elapsed time exceeds max_age.
prompt=none prevents interaction and requires an error when silent authentication cannot satisfy the request.

support_reference.claim: Phase 37 strictness includes durable max_age/auth_time handling.

cases.observed_outcome: 302/303 to the registered callback with login_required and original state.
cases.expected_outcome: Do not treat a stale host auth_time as fresh; return login_required without interaction under prompt=none.
cases.cause_detail: The deterministic host-session test passed for max_age=60 against stale auth_time.

repro.test_name: prompt=none plus stale auth_time under max_age returns login_required

cases.disposition: Existing deterministic source-host proof is reused; the host remains authoritative for account authentication time.

cases.provider_identity: GeneratedHostApp endpoint and test AccountResolver map host session auth_time into ID-token claims.

input_identity.request: Fresh host authentication time with max_age or explicit claims.id_token.auth_time request.

cases.profile: OIDC authorization code with host-owned session freshness
cases.auth_mode: public client with PKCE S256 and a fresh host session
cases.safe_condition: When max_age or explicit auth_time demand is met, emitted ID Token auth_time is an integer equal to the host-provided Unix second.

normative_references.basis: When max_age is used, the ID Token must include auth_time.

support_reference.claim: Phase 37 strictness includes integer auth_time emission when requested.

cases.observed_outcome: Both fresh max_age and explicit auth_time flows emit the configured integer auth_time claim.
cases.expected_outcome: ID Token includes integer auth_time matching the host-provided authentication time when required.
cases.cause_detail: The deterministic host integration test passed both request variants.

repro.test_name: fresh auth emits integer auth_time in the ID token when max_age or explicit auth_time demand is present

cases.disposition: Existing deterministic source-host proof is reused; this does not assert user-supplied or package auth_time policy.

cases.provider_identity: GeneratedHostApp Phoenix endpoint with Ecto test repository; Lockspire-issued urn:ietf:params:oauth:request_uri.

input_identity.request: Same public client submits the same issued request_uri to /authorize a second time after the first flow consumed it.

cases.safe_condition: One pushed reference is not reopened by replay after successful authorization-code use.

normative_references.basis: The client must use each request_uri once; expired references must be rejected.

support_reference.claim: Pushed authorization requests use Lockspire-issued request_uri references.

cases.observed_outcome: Second /authorize use returns HTTP 400 with request_uri invalid, expired, or already used.
cases.expected_outcome: A consumed request_uri cannot reopen the authorization flow.
cases.cause_detail: The required-PAR source integration test completed the first flow and rejected replay.

repro.test_name: required-PAR rejects direct authorize but still completes the canonical PAR auth-code plus PKCE flow

cases.disposition: Existing deterministic source-host proof is reused; no FAPI certification claim.

cases.provider_identity: Lockspire.Web.Router with two synthetic clients and durable PAR store.

input_identity.request: Client B submits Client A's valid request_uri to /authorize; synthetic credentials only.

cases.safe_condition: Only the posting client can use the resulting request_uri.

normative_references.basis: The request_uri value must be bound to the client that posted the authorization request.

support_reference.claim: PAR is supported as Lockspire-issued request_uri references.

cases.observed_outcome: Wrong-client use returns HTTP 400; the request_uri is burned and subsequent owner use is also rejected.
cases.expected_outcome: Reject a request_uri presented by a different client and prevent cross-client reuse.
cases.cause_detail: The current controller test verified rejection and burn behavior.

repro.test_name: wrong-client par attempts are rejected and burn the request_uri

cases.disposition: Existing deterministic source-host proof is reused.

cases.provider_identity: Lockspire.Web.Router controller test with synthetic already-expired PAR entry.

input_identity.request: The host stores a request_uri with expiry 600 seconds in the past, then receives it at /authorize.

cases.safe_condition: A stored request_uri is past its expires_at timestamp.

normative_references.basis: An expired request_uri must be rejected as invalid.

support_reference.claim: PAR references extend the existing authorization code + PKCE flow.

cases.observed_outcome: HTTP 400 first-party error; no redirect to a callback.
cases.expected_outcome: Reject an expired reference and do not continue authorization.
cases.cause_detail: The named browser-surface controller test passed.

repro.test_name: expired par request_uris fail safely at the browser surface

cases.disposition: Existing deterministic source-host proof is reused.

cases.provider_identity: GeneratedHostApp Phoenix endpoint with global required-PAR policy and host-owned consent flow.

input_identity.request: Compare direct /authorize without request_uri to a pushed request_uri flow for the same synthetic public client.

cases.profile: authorization code + PKCE with required PAR
cases.safe_condition: Global required-PAR policy rejects authorization data sent only front-channel, while a valid pushed request can complete the flow and token exchange.

normative_references.basis: Authorization Server policy may require PAR and refuse requests lacking a PAR-issued request_uri.
PAR endpoint errors use the OAuth error response format.

support_reference.claim: Global and client-specific PAR policies may be required or optional.

cases.observed_outcome: Direct request returns invalid_request and state to the exact callback; the pushed code+PKCE flow completes; replay is rejected.
cases.expected_outcome: Required-PAR rejects direct authorization data and permits the valid pushed flow.
cases.cause_detail: The named end-to-end source-host test passed both direct rejection and canonical pushed flow.

repro.test_name: required-PAR rejects direct authorize but still completes the canonical PAR auth-code plus PKCE flow

cases.disposition: Existing deterministic source-host policy evidence is reused.

cases.provider_identity: Lockspire.Web.Router source-host test host configured with the synthetic issuer and /lockspire consent mount.

input_identity.request: Two form PAR POSTs push scope openid email; reference-only control reaches consent; candidate adds only front-channel scope profile to a fresh reference.

cases.auth_mode: synthetic public client with PKCE S256
cases.safe_condition: The browser request presents parameters that disagree with values stored behind a valid pushed request_uri.

normative_references.basis: The returned request_uri references pushed authorization request data and directs its use in the authorization request.
Authorization request parameters may be duplicated between the request object and outer request.
The referenced request object is authoritative for duplicated parameters and client-ID equality remains required.
The integrity rationale protects request parameters from browser-front-channel modification.

support_reference.claim: PAR is supported as Lockspire-issued references extending the authorization code + PKCE flow.

cases.observed_outcome: The reference-only control reaches consent with pushed openid/email; the candidate conflicting outer scope receives HTTP 400 before consent.
cases.expected_outcome: The valid reference reaches consent using pushed openid/email, ignoring outer scope=profile without union or override.
cases.cause_detail: Both independent PAR POSTs and the reference-only consent control passed; the conflicting outer scope request was rejected with HTTP 400 before consent instead of using the pushed scope. Settled scope interpretation is attributed in 171-QUALIFICATION-DECISIONS.md; the completed controlled HTTP observation reproduces the blanket rejection.

repro.test_name: P171-005 valid pushed-reference control requires pushed scopes to remain authoritative over front-channel scope
repro.reason: Both independent PAR POSTs and the reference-only consent control passed; the conflicting outer scope request was rejected with HTTP 400 before consent instead of using the pushed scope.

cases.disposition: A current supported normative failure was reproduced with valid controls; carry it as correction input to the downstream owner.

policy_interpretation.decision: For a valid Lockspire-issued reference, the pushed scope is authoritative; ignore the duplicate outer scope without merging or overriding it.
policy_interpretation.basis: Linked-clause interpretation: RFC 9126 Section 4 incorporates RFC 9101 request semantics; RFC 9101 Sections 5 and 6.3 establish duplicate and authoritative parameter handling, and Section 10.7 explains the integrity rationale. This is not a direct quotation from RFC 9126.
boundaries: PAR may be plain form-encoded; no JWT/JAR requirement is introduced.
request and request_uri remain mutually exclusive.

normative_references.basis: Provider metadata identifies the issuer and endpoint locations used by relying parties.

support_reference.claim: OIDC discovery and truthful FAPI metadata are part of the supported surface.

cases.expected_outcome: Advertised issuer and endpoint metadata match the configured issuer and mounted route shape.
cases.cause_detail: Seven discovery controller tests passed, including truthful mounted metadata; this does not exercise external reverse-proxy/TLS/browser reachability.
cases.disposition: Current source-host metadata proof passes; external issuer/TLS/proxy/browser reachability remains excluded pending an available exact-input profile run.
